subject: Service disruption: executive update and remediation roadmap
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@polarishealth.com>, Polaris Health Ops <ops@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: Service disruption: immediate update

Hi Sanjay / Polaris Ops team,

We saw an elevated error rate impacting API responses for requests routed to the us-west region starting ~08:45 PT this morning. Our on-call team opened a bridge at 08:58 PT; I wanted to provide an immediate, high-level update while we continue diagnostics and mitigation.

Impact: a subset of generation requests from your production cluster experienced 5xx errors and increased latency. We estimate 12% of your requests in the 08:45–09:05 window were affected.

What we are doing now:
- Active bridge (ENG, SRE, Account team) investigating root cause.
- Rolling a limited fallback to the compatible model variant to restore throughput while preserving model fidelity.
- Capturing full request traces and KV cache state; attaching a short timeline as we build one.

Attachments: polaris_incident_timeline.pdf (initial timeline stub)

Next update by 10:00 PT or sooner if we have a significant change. We will also share a technical summary and remediation plan once we've stabilized.

Appreciate your patience — we're treating this as a Sev1 and prioritized across the stack.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@polarishealth.com>, Polaris Health Ops <ops@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14 10:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption: immediate update (executive summary)

Sanjay — quick executive summary and immediate remediation steps based on current bridge findings.

Summary (as of 10:00 PT):
- Incident start: ~08:45 PT.
- Symptom: sudden increase in tokenization-related CPU spikes on a narrow subset of model shards handling requests with long context (>6k tokens). This led to backpressure in the request queue and cascading 5xx errors.
- Scope: affected ~12% of your requests for ~20 minutes; not all regions; us-west routing table had higher concentration.

Immediate actions taken:
1) Rollback to a compatible quantized model slice (v2-q8) for impacted shards — restored baseline throughput by ~75% within 9 minutes of rollout.
2) Activated prefix KV-cache bypass for long-context requests to reduce KV pressure.
3) Elevated resource schedules on Dedicated pool to accept queued requests.

Customer impact and data integrity:
- No persisted user data was modified by the runtime. In-flight requests that returned 5xx were retried by your client or dropped; we have request traces and will provide a list of request IDs for correlation.
- We do not see evidence of corrupted storage or logs.

ETA: We expect to reach normal error rates within the hour, barring new regressions. We will confirm when we've observed 60 minutes of stable traffic post-remediation.

Compensation and next steps:
- We will fast-track a detailed postmortem and a remediation roadmap within 72 hours.
- As a gesture for the disruption, we will propose a one-time credit for affected tokens; details to be shared in the postmortem.

I will set a 15:30 PT call if you'd like to walk through the technical timeline and mitigation.

— Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: polaris_incident_timeline.pdf (updated)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@polarishealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-14 11:30 -0700
Subject: RE: Service disruption: quick technical notes

Hannah — posting the short technical notes we shared on the bridge for the record.

Key debugging observations:
- The problematic requests all included unusually long system prompts and 1:1000 sampling of a customer debug header that caused KV cache pressure during decode.
- One of the kernel paths we use for q8 quantization had a rare edge-case where memory reclamation was delayed under sustained long-sequence attention; this contributed to transient CPU thrashing on the affected shard.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Bypass the incremental KV refresh for flagged requests.
- Patch queued, tested, and staged a kernel fix to remove the delayed reclamation; will push to canary tonight after extended test cycles.

Artifacts attached: initial_root_cause_notes.txt (engineering notes)

— David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@polarishealth.com>, Polaris Health Ops <ops@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14 15:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Service disruption: executive summary and remediation roadmap

Sanjay — we’ve stabilized service and are now in validation. Key items:

What is stabilized:
- Baseline error rates returned to normal by ~10:20 PT after the model-slice rollback and KV bypass.
- Queues drained and latency returned to expected SLOs across affected hosts.

Planned remediation roadmap (next 72 hours):
1) Full root cause analysis (RCA) draft — due 2028-06-16 10:00 PT.
2) Kernel patch canary and validation on limited fleet — targeting 2028-06-16 evening.
3) Wider rollout contingent on canary results; we will share rollout schedule and risk window.
4) Customer-specific tunings (prefix handling) to reduce long-context pressure — opt-in config we can enable for Polaris after your approval.

Immediate asks for Polaris:
- Please confirm if you want Redwood to enable the optional prefix handling tuning for your account (we can enable with a rollback plan).
- If you want a lobby call with your CTO, we can schedule it 16:00–16:30 PT today.

Compensation: we will include a credits proposal in the RCA packet; we can escalate to Sales for faster approval if you prefer.

I’ve attached the incident timeline and preliminary root cause notes. We will follow up with a formal postmortem and action-tracking board.

— Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Attachment: polaris_incident_timeline.pdf (finalized), initial_root_cause_notes.txt

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@polarishealth.com>, Polaris Health Ops <ops@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15 16:45 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: postmortem publication and tracked actions (INC-1023)

Sanjay — thanks again for your patience and the productive bridge yesterday. We published the RCA and the tracked action board for INC-1023. Highlights and links below.

What we found (TL;DR):
- A rare interaction between long-context requests and a delayed memory reclamation path in the q8 kernel produced transient CPU thrash and queue pressure on a narrow set of shards; this produced elevated 5xxs during a ~20 minute window.

Customer-facing commitments we delivered:
- Kernel patch merged and validated on canary; full fleet rollout scheduled for 2028-06-17 (risk window included).
- Optional prefix-handling tuning prepared; we can enable it for Polaris with a planned roll and rollback.
- We propose a one-time credit covering the affected tokens. Our Sales lead will follow up to confirm the amount; we have fast-tracked approval.

Action items (tracked):
- RED-INC-1023-1: Roll canary kernel patch — owner: David Kim — ETA 2028-06-16 22:00 PT.
- RED-INC-1023-2: Fleet rollout & monitoring runbook — owner: Marcus Lin — ETA 2028-06-17 12:00 PT.
- RED-INC-1023-3: Customer opt-in prefix tuning (if approved) — owner: Monica Patel — ETA 2028-06-18 09:00 PT.
- RED-INC-1023-4: Credits proposal submitted to Sales — owner: Hannah Schmitt — ETA 2028-06-15 18:00 PT.

Public artifacts:
- Postmortem (RCA): https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/INC-1023
- Tracked actions & timeline: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/incident-logs-pol-1023

If you’d like a final walkthrough with our engineering leadership before rollout, we can schedule a 30-minute session on 2028-06-16.

Thanks again — we understand the disruption and are committed to preventing recurrence.

— Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
